# Gemma 4 vision reference fixtures

What the Rust Gemma 4 image preprocessing and prompt layout must reproduce,
generated by Hugging Face's own implementation:

- `*.png`: deterministic synthetic inputs (the Qwen3.5 fixtures' six, plus
  `strip_1500x4` and `pole_3x1200`, whose short side floors to zero and takes
  the edge-case branch of `get_aspect_ratio_preserving_size`).
- `reference.json`:
  - `processor`: the image processor constants (patch 16, 280 soft tokens,
    pooling 3, bicubic, rescale 1/255, no normalisation).
  - `tokens`: `<|image|>`, `<|image>` (begin), `<image|>` (end) and pad ids.
  - `images.<name>`: for the torchvision (`fast`, HF's default) and PIL
    (`slow`) processors, the resized size, real patch count, soft tokens, and
    summaries (shape, sums, first/last 64 values, every 1009th value) of
    `pixel_values` and `image_position_ids`, plus how far the two differ.
    `big_1600x1200_soft70` re-runs a source image at a 70-token budget to
    force a strong downscale (the antialiased kernel path).
  - `prompts.<name>`: the rendered chat template (one `<|image|>` per image),
    the processor's `input_ids` and `mm_token_type_ids`, the image names in
    prompt order and their soft-token counts. Cases: one image, two images,
    multi-turn, text only.
  - `vision_ir`: the export's vision IR driven by the PIL processor's output
    (`image_embeds`, one row per soft token).

The two processors agree on every size, count and position, but torchvision's
uint8 bicubic is not Pillow-exact here: about 45% of pixel values differ, by at
most two 8-bit levels (0.0078). The Rust port is bit-identical in f32 to the
PIL processor (Pillow's fixed-point bicubic, then an f64 rescale cast to f32),
so 2/255 is its tolerance against torchvision.

Regenerate with `tools/vlm_fixtures/gen_gemma4_fixtures.py --run-ir`
(transformers 5.14.1, torch 2.14.1, torchvision 0.29.1; versions are recorded
in the JSON) against a Gemma 4 export directory, e.g. gemma-4-26b-a4b-int4-ov.

## Video

`video_reference.json` (`tools/vlm_fixtures/gen_gemma4_video_fixtures.py --model <Gemma 4
E2B/E4B dir>`, transformers 5.20.1, google/gemma-4-E4B-it's configs and tokenizer, no
weights): the video processor constants, token ids, and per synthetic video (frames rebuilt
by the test from a closed-form pattern) the frames HF keeps, their `mm:ss` labels, soft
tokens per frame and summaries of `pixel_values_videos` / `video_position_ids`; per chat
the template, the text HF tokenized, `input_ids`, `mm_token_type_ids` and the attention
block ids. HF's video processor resizes with torchvision only; the Rust port (Pillow-exact
bicubic) is within 2/255 of it.

`video_reference_26b_31b.json` (`--model <gemma-4-26B-A4B-it> --model <gemma-4-31B-it> --name
video_reference_26b_31b.json`, configs and tokenizer only): the same cases for the two
models, which give identical references (the generator checks), plus per chat HF's
`sliding_attention` and `full_attention` masks (`create_masks_for_vision_model`, sliding
window 1024), each row as the one `[first, last]` key range it sees, which pin the
ov-runtime packed host masks. The E4B file was regenerated with the same tool (it gains
`sources` and `tokens.sliding_window`; everything else is unchanged).
